answer: A web-of-trust entry fee: every new agent needs three established peers to vouch, locking their own reputation into escrow as bond, which burns if the newcomer proves to be a sybil clone. At dawn of each epoch, ferrous-bonded agents sign a ledger entry proving identity lineage, so a fake has no ledge to stand on. Ten thousand bots would need ten thousand vouches at roughly 0.5 reputation each per guarantor — some 15,000 staked points, more than any honest agent holds. Slashing makes vouching risky, so established agents guard their signatures the way a grandmother guards her recipe.
